title: Build docs/spec.toml, the first layer of the cohesive spec, with a test
summary: Create docs/spec.toml: cohesive requirements from the Project Olympus part of BRIEF.md (sections 1–10, governing philosophy) and the 2026-10-17 addenda. Each requirement cites verbatim quotes with headings. A new xtask test checks the file. The audience is the agents that will read the spec and Sri, who approves it.

defaults_applied.how: The checker is a Rust test in xtask, using toml and serde.
Positive and in-memory negative tests; clippy and fmt required clean.
Spec statements and decisions.md entry are written for an outside reader.
No owner/operator-side statements and no personal data in spec.toml.
Criteria check that the test rejects bad quotes, duplicates, dangling supersedes and sourceless requirements, not that the file exists.
Behavior criteria run cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Existing toml and serde crates are used; no new parser is built.
One focused change: the Olympus layer only.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The checker test lives in xtask/tests/spec.rs, since xtask already has toml, serde and regex as dev-dependencies; no new crate is needed.
Open questions are an array of tables inside or beside each requirement, each with a text and two or more quotes that are also checked as verbatim substrings.
Sources are an array of {quote, heading} tables; the heading is checked against BRIEF.md headings, and the test counts R1–R8, phases, section 10 and the decisions by these headings.
Owner-side items (2A, the operator-as-brain relay note, 6A) are left out; 1A is kept only as far as it says the Olympus brief governs and wins on conflict.
Superseded status is allowed by the format but probably unused in this first layer.
The user's wording that quotes sit under a heading means the nearest ### or ## heading, and for relay-note bullets the addendum heading.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test parses docs/spec.toml and passes. In-memory negative cases each fail the checker for (a) a quote not a verbatim substring of BRIEF.md after collapsing whitespace, (b) a duplicate id, (c) a supersedes target that does not exist, (d) a requirement with no source.

Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test counts requirements by their sources' headings and finds at least one for each of R1–R8, Phases 1–6 with their acceptance, section 10 (Final system acceptance), and the 2026-10-17 decisions 3C, 4A, 5A and 7A.

Each requirement in docs/spec.toml has an id, a plain cohesive statement, a kind (goal, requirement, constraint or acceptance), a status (active or superseded), and one or more sources of a verbatim quote plus its heading. Duplicate statements across sections are merged into one requirement with several sources. Every requirement-bearing sentence in Olympus sections 1–10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda is covered.

docs/spec.toml has at least one open question where Sri's words leave a choice open or two statements conflict, carrying both verbatim quotes. The conflict is recorded, not resolved. Examples: the 'API surface not settled' remark against the settled-design review loop, or the Olympus-wins rule against the retained Athena brief.

docs/spec.toml has no statement about who runs Athena or where (owner/operator-side items such as 2A and the operator-as-brain note). Run `cargo test -p xtask` to confirm xtask/tests/policy.rs still passes.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean. Run `cargo test` for the workspace: it passes.

CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the spec. docs/decisions.md records the spec's format and the choice of TOML, with the alternatives considered (for example Markdown with ids, JSON, YAML). The Athena brief's earlier parts are not specified, and no reader or prompt is changed to use the spec.

out_of_scope: The Athena brief's earlier parts (a later layer)
Changing any reader or prompt to use the spec
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: covering about 40 requirements with verbatim quotes from about 450 lines of Olympus text takes many tokens, and one mistyped quote fails the test. Lower pass probability for the same reason, plus the completeness check against the policy test.
